# B-Roll Animation: "Why This Matters" Section

**Duration:** ~85 seconds (00:00:00:00 - 00:01:25:01)
**Format:** One continuous Remotion composition
**Resolution:** 1920x1080, 30fps
**Style:** Mock UI elements, data viz, abstract icons. Apify brand colors.

---

## Part 1: Raw Description (Shot-by-Shot)

### Beat 1: AEO is the next frontier (0:00 - 0:04)
Text "AEO" animates in large, bold, center screen. Below it, a subtle horizon line draws itself across the frame. Small icons (magnifying glass, AI chip, chat bubble) float up past the horizon like rising stars. Sets the tone: something new is emerging.

### Beat 2: AI engines pick passages, cite sources (0:04 - 0:13)
Transition into a mock SERP layout. A simplified Google-style results page appears with 10 blurred result cards stacked vertically. An AI "scanner" highlight sweeps down the page, but instead of stopping at #1, it pulls a glowing text fragment out of result #7 and #10. The fragments float to the right side of the screen and slot into a clean "AI Answer" card that assembles itself. Source citations appear as small pills below the answer card.

### Beat 3: #10 cited, #1 ignored (0:13 - 0:21)
The SERP view simplifies. Result #1 is prominent at the top, result #10 is small at the bottom. A spotlight/glow lands on #10, which scales up slightly. Result #1 dims and gets a subtle strikethrough or fade. A citation arrow draws from #10 to the AI Answer card. #1 gets a "not cited" X icon. Visual contrast: the underdog wins.

### Beat 4: Existing tools are expensive (0:21 - 0:29)
Scene shifts to a pricing comparison. Three columns appear representing "Specialized AEO Platform", "Semrush/Ahrefs Higher Tier", and a third blank slot. Price tags animate in: "$$$" and "$$" with dollar amounts ($300+/mo, $200+/mo). The columns have a muted, slightly negative color treatment (grays, dull reds). A lock icon sits on the Semrush/Ahrefs column to represent gated features.

### Beat 5: Apify pricing (0:29 - 0:42)
The third column lights up with the Apify brand color. "$2 / 1,000 results" types in. A simple bar chart or comparison graphic slides in showing the cost difference visually (tall bars for competitors, tiny bar for Apify). Below, three small badges pop in: "Google AI Mode", "Perplexity", "ChatGPT", showing you get all three. The Apify column pulses or glows to draw attention.

### Beat 6: What you can do with the data (0:42 - 1:09)
This is the longest beat, so it flows through sub-scenes:

**6a - Compare engines (0:42 - 0:54)**
Three vertical panels slide in side by side, labeled "Google AI Mode", "Perplexity", "ChatGPT". Each panel has a simplified AI answer card with different source citations highlighted. Colored lines or connectors draw between matching sources across panels. Some sources appear in all three (highlighted green), some in only one (highlighted amber). A "gap" indicator pulses on the panel where your brand is missing.

**6b - Track competitors (0:54 - 1:03)**
The three panels compress to the top of the frame. Below, a simplified timeline/trend chart draws itself. Multiple lines represent different domains. Your competitor's line is climbing, yours is flat or absent. Annotation labels pop in: "Competitor A: cited 12x", "You: cited 2x". Shows the competitive intelligence angle.

**6c - Content format preference (1:03 - 1:09)**
A horizontal bar chart or icon grid shows content types: "Listicle", "How-To Guide", "Comparison", "Long-form". Bars fill to different lengths showing which format AI engines prefer. The winning format gets a checkmark or glow.

### Beat 7: Multi-country support (1:09 - 1:25)
A simplified world map or globe graphic fades in. Three location pins drop onto US, Germany, Japan. Each pin expands into a small card showing a different AI answer for the same query, with different sources cited. The cards are visually distinct (different citations highlighted) to show regional variation. Final moment: all three cards are visible simultaneously, reinforcing the cross-market comparison capability.

---

## Part 2: Remotion Code-Gen Prompt

```
Create a single continuous Remotion composition (1920x1080, 30fps, ~85 seconds / 2550 frames) for an Apify YouTube video b-roll animation. This covers the "Why This Matters" section about Answer Engine Optimization (AEO).

Design system:
- Background: dark (#1A1A2E or similar deep navy/charcoal)
- Primary accent: Apify brand blue (#00AAFF) for highlights and CTAs
- Secondary accents: green (#4ADE80) for positive indicators, amber (#FBBF24) for warnings, red/gray (#9CA3AF) for negative indicators
- Typography: clean sans-serif (Inter or similar), white text on dark background
- Motion style: smooth easeInOut transitions, elements slide/fade in with purpose, no bounce or overly playful easing
- UI elements should look like simplified, stylized mockups, not pixel-perfect screenshots

The animation flows through these phases continuously (frame counts approximate at 30fps):

PHASE 1 (frames 0-120): "AEO" text animates in center screen, large and bold. A horizontal line draws across below it. Small floating icons (magnifying glass, AI chip, chat bubble) rise past the line. Establishing shot.

PHASE 2 (frames 120-390): Transition to a mock SERP layout with 10 blurred result cards stacked vertically. An AI scanner highlight sweeps down the results. It pulls glowing text fragments from results #7 and #10 (not #1). The fragments float rightward and assemble into an "AI Answer" card with citation pills underneath.

PHASE 3 (frames 390-630): SERP simplifies to show just #1 (top, prominent) and #10 (bottom, small). Spotlight lands on #10, which scales up. #1 dims/fades. A citation arrow draws from #10 to the AI Answer card. #1 gets an X icon. Visual: underdog wins.

PHASE 4 (frames 630-870): Pricing comparison with three columns. "AEO Platform" ($300+/mo) and "Semrush/Ahrefs" ($200+/mo, with lock icon) appear in muted colors. The third column is empty, building anticipation.

PHASE 5 (frames 870-1260): Third column lights up with Apify accent color. "$2 / 1,000 results" types in. A bar chart shows the cost difference (tall bars vs tiny bar). Three badges pop in below: "Google AI Mode", "Perplexity", "ChatGPT".

PHASE 6a (frames 1260-1620): Three vertical panels labeled "Google AI Mode", "Perplexity", "ChatGPT". Each has a simplified AI answer with different citations. Colored lines connect matching sources across panels. Green = appears in all, amber = appears in one. A "gap" indicator pulses where the user's brand is missing.

PHASE 6b (frames 1620-1890): Panels compress upward. A timeline chart draws below with multiple domain trend lines. Competitor line rises, user's line is flat. Annotations: "Competitor A: cited 12x" vs "You: cited 2x".

PHASE 6c (frames 1890-2070): Horizontal bar chart of content formats (Listicle, How-To, Comparison, Long-form). Bars fill to different lengths. Top format gets a checkmark glow.

PHASE 7 (frames 2070-2550): Simplified world map/globe fades in. Location pins drop on US, Germany, Japan. Each pin expands into a card showing a different AI answer with different citations. All three cards visible at end, reinforcing cross-market comparison. Fade out.

Use useCurrentFrame() and interpolate() for all timing. Use spring() for element entrances. Keep transitions between phases smooth, crossfading or sliding between scenes. Each phase should feel like a natural continuation, not a hard cut.
```

---

## Notes

- The frame counts are approximate. Adjust to match the actual subtitle timing once placed on the timeline.
- If the Remotion composition ends up too complex for a single file, split into 2-3 compositions (Phases 1-3, 4-5, 6-7) and stitch in the editor.
- The mock UI elements should be stylized/simplified, not realistic screenshots. We want the viewer to get the concept, not read actual text.

Fix the following issues while keeping the existing graphics and animation structure intact. Do not redesign scenes, just adjust sizing, spacing, and layout.

1. SCALE UP SMALL ELEMENTS
Many elements (cards, citation pills, chart labels, map pins, country cards) are too small relative to the 3840x2160 canvas. Scale them up so they're clearly readable at YouTube playback size, including when downscaled to 1080p. As a rule of thumb, no card or UI element should be narrower than ~700px, and no text should be smaller than 36px.

2. REDUCE WASTED SPACE IN CARDS (Phase 6a - "Compare Citations Across AI Engines")
The three engine cards (Google AI Mode, Perplexity, ChatGPT) have too much empty padding inside. Tighten the internal spacing: reduce vertical padding between the skeleton text lines, the "CITATIONS" label, and the citation pills. The cards should feel compact and dense, not stretched out. Also, lay out the three cards SIDE BY SIDE horizontally instead of stacked vertically, so they fill the width of the frame and allow direct visual comparison.

3. REMOVE ALL SECTION HEADING TEXTS AT THE TOP
Delete the title text that appears at the top of each scene (e.g. "Compare Citations Across AI Engines", "Track AI Citations Across Countries & Languages", etc.). The narration already explains what the viewer is looking at. The headings are redundant and take up vertical space. Just remove them entirely, and let the graphics use that reclaimed space.

Fix the following three issues. Keep all existing graphics, animations, and colors. Only adjust layout and sizing.

1. CITATION COMPARISON SCENE (Phase 6a - three engine cards)
The three cards stretch edge to edge and feel too wide for their content. Reduce card width so each card is around 900-1000px wide. Lay them out SIDE BY SIDE in a horizontal row, centered on the canvas, with ~40px gaps between them. This will make the comparison feel tighter and more intentional. The skeleton text lines and citation pills inside should scale proportionally to the new card width.

2. LINE CHART SCENE (Phase 6b - AI Citation Frequency)
The chart container is only taking up roughly the left half of the frame, leaving the entire right side empty. Expand the chart container to fill the full width of the canvas (with normal padding, ~80px on each side). The line graph, x-axis labels, and legend should all stretch to use the full available width. Center the whole thing vertically on the canvas as well.

3. WORLD MAP SCENE (Phase 7 - countries)
The map and country cards are still too small, sitting in the center with massive empty space around them. Scale the entire map graphic up by at least 1.5x so it fills most of the canvas width. The country cards (United States, Germany, Japan) should also scale up proportionally and remain anchored to their respective pin locations on the map. The map should feel immersive, not like a thumbnail.

Two changes. Keep all existing graphics, animations, and timing intact. 1. REPLACE BACKGROUND Remove the current solid color background and the subtle grid overlay. Instead, use a static image file called "background_blue.png" as the full-canvas background (3840x2160, no scaling needed, it's already the right size). Use staticFile() to load it and render it as an behind everything else. 2. SAFE ZONE: SCALE ALL CONTENT TO FIT WITHIN 210px MARGINS All animated content (cards, charts, text, map, icons, everything except the background image) must fit within a safe zone of 210px from every edge of the canvas. That means the usable area is 3420x1740, starting at position (210, 210). Wrap all scene content in a container div positioned at left: 210, top: 210, with width: 3420 and height: 1740, and set overflow: hidden. Then scale down any elements that currently extend beyond this area. Do not change the aspect ratio or relative positioning of elements within scenes, just make sure nothing bleeds outside the 210px margin on any side.
one last thing - no fade in animation in the beggining pls

The only change made was removing the opening `BlackScreen` sequence and its associated fade-in transition from `MainComposition`. The composition now starts directly on `Phase1` at frame 0 with no fade-in — the AEO text springs in immediately. The closing fade-out to black at the end is preserved. The `durationInFrames` export was also updated to account for the removed 20-frame black screen (2605 → 2585), but since the sequence math already nets out correctly with the transition overlaps, the total stays consistent.

Animation generated — preview is live.

Change the frame rate from 30fps to 25fps. This requires the following adjustments:

1. Set `export const fps = 25;`
2. Multiply ALL spring() delay values by 25/30 (round to nearest integer)
3. Multiply ALL interpolate() frame ranges by 25/30 (round to nearest integer)
4. Multiply ALL TransitionSeries.Sequence durationInFrames values by 25/30 (round to nearest integer)
5. Set TRANSITION to Math.round(20 * 25/30) = 17
6. Recalculate durationInFrames to match the new total
7. Do NOT change any visual properties (colors, sizes, positions, easing configs, opacity values). Only timing-related values change.
